segments.he: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לֵית לְהוּ, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: אִית לְהוּ. מִי לָא אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שָׁחוֹר — אָדוֹם הוּא, אֶלָּא שֶׁלָּקָה? הָכִי נָמֵי, מִלְקָא הוּא דְּלָקֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «If you wish, say» that Beit Shammai «do not accept» this opinion of Rabbi Abbahu, and they maintain that there are more than four types of blood in a woman. «And if you wish, say» instead that Beit Shammai «do accept» Rabbi Abbahu’s exposition, and the apparent contradiction can be resolved as follows: «Didn’t Rabbi Ḥanina say» with regard to the «black» blood mentioned in the mishna that it is not an additional type, as it «is» actually «red but» its color «has faded? So too,» with regard to the colors of blood mentioned by Beit Shammai, that of water in which a fenugreek plant is soaked, and that of the liquid that drips from roast meat, one can say that these are not additional types of blood. Rather, they too were initially red but their color «faded.»
